# Critique — Pattern 2 (Metabolic)

The slot allocation across the 255 slots was distributed as follows: Diagnosed Conditions (~15%), Treatments/Interventions (~10%), Weight & Body Composition (~10%), Lipids (~5%), Symptoms (~20%), Family History (~10%), Self-Monitoring & Labs (~15%), and Lifestyle (~15%). A few self-monitoring questions toward the end (e.g., positions 250–255) felt slightly forced to reach the 255-question limit; had the limit been larger, more specific thyroid and autoimmune symptoms would have been detailed. Significant overlap exists with the Cardiovascular and Nutrition domains (e.g., lipids, statins, sugar intake) as metabolic risk directly translates to cardiovascular disease and is driven by diet. The V-flag was applied to questions where a "Yes" indicates a healthy behavior or favorable metric (e.g., tracking macros, recent testing, dietary improvements) to support a downstream convention where a stored bit `1` represents risk or abnormality. We drew inspiration from the ADA Diabetes Risk Test and FINDRISC, which we paraphrased; clinicians seeking formal risk scores should refer to the original validated ADA tools. The weakest question is position 255 ("Do you feel empowered and in control...") as it measures subjective psychological state rather than physiological markers. There was no prior question art in `patterns.json` for Pattern 2, allowing a clean, customized draft from the ground up.
